subject.title: feat(telegram): show quiet-tool progress draft in partial streaming mode

question: Should Telegram partial mode intentionally stop rendering immediate tool-progress previews in favor of a two-minute quiet fallback, or should quiet feedback preserve the existing partial-mode progress contract?
rationale: Current docs, tests, and resolver defaults define immediate partial-mode tool progress as existing behavior, while the PR intentionally changes that user-visible default; that is a compatibility/product decision even if the liveness goal is valid.

options.title: Preserve Partial Progress
options.body: Keep existing immediate `preview.toolProgress` behavior and layer quiet-turn feedback only where no current preview path can render visible output.

options.title: Redefine Partial Mode
options.body: Accept the delayed prose-first policy, then update docs/release notes and add explicit upgrade and live Telegram proof for the changed default.

options.title: Pause For Scope Decision
options.body: Hold this PR until the linked Telegram liveness issue decides whether the fix should be a quiet fallback, a session command, or part of ingress-lane redesign.

recommendation.title: Preserve Partial Progress
recommendation.body: Keep existing immediate `preview.toolProgress` behavior and layer quiet-turn feedback only where no current preview path can render visible output.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked liveness issue and the recent merged progress-draft/current-default implementation that this PR changes.
